net.title: Fast metering
net.description: Optional: the EMS reads the HomeWizard P1 meter directly every second, within your own network. Enter its IP address; the local API must be enabled in the HomeWizard app. Without an address the EMS follows the Home Assistant sensor (every 5 seconds), which is plenty for switching heat buffers.

data.p1_host: IP address of the HomeWizard P1 meter (optional)

tarieven.title: Tariffs
tarieven.description: With a fixed tariff only the two fixed prices apply. With a dynamic tariff choose a sensor with hourly prices in its attributes (Nord Pool, ENTSO-e or your supplier). Prices decide which hours count as expensive in the outlook.

data.salderen: Net metering (export is worth as much as import)
data.price_scale: Conversion factor to EUR/kWh (0.001 for EUR/MWh)

warmtepomp.title: Heat pump and weather
warmtepomp.description: With its own kWh counter and an outdoor temperature sensor the EMS learns how much the heat pump uses at which temperature. The weather forecast then gives the expected heating use. Hours in which the EMS had raised the thermostat are left out.

accu.title: Battery
accu.description:
The EMS does not control the battery: set it to its own self-consumption mode (zero at the meter). The EMS only reads charge and power, predicts when it will be full and empty, and lets heat buffers take sun only once the battery has enough.

Virtual: the battery exists only in the calculation and follows the P1 meter like a real battery in self-consumption, so you can see what it would do before buying one.

Zendure: read locally via the zenSDK; only the IP address is needed.

Via entities: any other battery, via the sensors of its own integration. The state of charge is required; power keeps the load model clean and shows whether the battery would feed a buffer.

data.name: Name
data.host: Zendure: IP address of the battery
data.power_invert: Power sensor is inverted (+ is discharging)

verbruiker.title: Consumer with its own model
verbruiker.description:
For a consumer with its own kWh counter, such as a hot tub or charger. The EMS does not control it but learns its use per hour of day and per outdoor temperature and includes that in the forecast.

If it has a thermostat, also choose the set and measured temperature. The EMS then learns how much it uses when at temperature and when calling for heat, and adjusts the next hours accordingly.

thermostaat.title: Shift: thermostat
thermostaat.description:
With surplus solar the EMS temporarily raises the set temperature. The heat pump keeps running and stores heat in the floor; the heating curve stays untouched. Afterwards the EMS restores the previous temperature. If someone (or a schedule) changes the thermostat meanwhile, the EMS leaves it.

The battery comes first: the buffer may only start once the battery has the minimum charge and there is still enough left. Battery discharge counts as a shortfall, so the battery never feeds the heat pump.

Without a thermostat entity the EMS only gives a signal (binary sensor '… vrijgegeven').

data.name: Name
data.boost_c: Raise by this many degrees on surplus
data.power_w: Expected heat pump power while running
data.min_soc_pct: Only once the battery is at least this full
data.end_hour: At the latest until (hour of day)
data.need_forecast: Only if the forecast shows enough surplus for the minimum run time
data.on_delay_min: On: surplus must last this long
data.off_delay_min: Off: surplus may fall short this long
data.rest_min: Off when it draws nothing for this long (0 = don't watch)

schakelaar.title: Shift: switch
schakelaar.description:
A heating element, such as the one in the boiler, is switched on while there is enough solar left after the battery. The tank's own thermostat remains the hard limit; a temperature sensor allows stopping earlier.

The battery comes first, and battery discharge counts as a shortfall. With a power sensor the EMS sees when the tank is at temperature (the element draws nothing) and passes the surplus to the next load.

Without a switch entity the EMS only gives a signal (binary sensor '… vrijgegeven').

data.energy: Consumption (kWh counter, optional; keeps this use out of the load model)

data.end_hour: At the latest until (hour of day)
data.need_forecast: Only if the forecast shows enough surplus for the minimum run time
data.on_delay_min: On: surplus must last this long
data.off_delay_min: Off: surplus may fall short this long
data.rest_min: Off when it draws nothing for this long (0 = don't watch)
